title: Map analysis tasks to rubric-defined metrics and dimensions
when_to_use: When the task instructions or rubric explicitly define specific formulas, indicators, or a scoring framework
experience:
*   Before coding, extract all required metrics and dimensions from the task description and any scoring rubric.
*   Verify that your planned calculations match the exact definitions (formulas, data sources, aggregations) provided.
*   If the rubric offers multiple analysis paths (e.g., Path A, Path B), explicitly choose one and note your choice.
*   Structure your code to compute the required metrics as separate, clearly labeled variables or columns.
*   Validate your final outputs against the rubric's expected metric names and calculation logic.
checklist: Extract all rubric-specified metrics and formulas
Compare planned calculations to rubric definitions
Explicitly select an analysis path if multiple are defined
Code and label metrics according to rubric names
common_failure_prevented: Producing analysis based on self-derived metrics that do not satisfy the task's defined evaluation criteria.

title: Verify data schema and joins align with analysis entities
when_to_use: When the analysis requires linking records across multiple tables to compute per-entity metrics
experience:
*   Before writing complex joins, map the primary key/foreign key relationships between all relevant tables.
*   Explicitly check for one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many relationships that could cause duplication or incorrect aggregations.
*   Test join logic on a small sample to verify it produces the expected grain (e.g., one row per user, per login event).
*   When calculating rates (e.g., incidents per user), ensure the denominator (e.g., user count) is derived from the correct, non-duplicated source table.
checklist: Test join logic on a sample
Verify aggregation grain matches metric definition
common_failure_prevented: Incorrectly joining tables leading to miscounted numerators or denominators for rates and proportions.

title: Prioritize rubric-specified analysis paths over novel methodologies
when_to_use: When a scoring rubric provides specific, graded analysis methods or answer patterns
experience:
*   Identify if the rubric provides 'paths' (e.g., Path A, Path B) with associated scores or reference answers.
*   Before devising a novel analytical method, check if your planned approach aligns with one of the provided paths.
*   If your novel method diverges, explicitly justify why the rubric path is insufficient or incorrect for the task.
*   When in doubt, implement the rubric's specified method first to ensure baseline task compliance, then add novel analysis as supplementary.
checklist: Identify all predefined analysis paths in the rubric
Compare your planned method to the predefined paths
Justify any deviation from the rubric's methods
Implement the rubric's method as a primary baseline
common_failure_prevented: Developing a creative but ungraded analysis that results in a score of zero for not following the required method.
